notes: Adopted four practices from the sibling NetAppModeler project (a client-side ASUP-parsing tool), following a comparative review of what would genuinely transfer. (1) ASUP parser strengthened: tools/asup_parser.py now parses licenses.xml (structured license entitlement export, including demo/expired detection), aggr-info.xml (byte-accurate aggregate capacity, overriding text-only 'aggr status -r' dumps that carry no capacity numbers at all), SAS Host Adapter port lines from sysconfig -a dumps (previously unparsed -- a different line shape than Ethernet ports), and storage-shelf.xml/STORAGE-SHELF.txt shelf inventory (product_id/serial_number cross-reference). All four are real formats confirmed present in real customer ASUP bundles per NetAppModeler's own changelog, translated from its JS parser to Python, not guessed at. (2) New PLATFORM_COVERAGE.md traceability document consolidating every confirmed-vs-unconfirmed hardware/switch/MetroCluster data point established this session, matching NetAppModeler's sourcing-discipline pattern. (3) Added a real-data-driven, non-scoring MTU/jumbo-frame check on data-role network ports (concept ported from NetAppModeler's Rule 22), using the already-harvested maxTransmissionUnitBytes field -- informational only, does not affect the Feature Adoption Score. (4) New automated regression test suite (tests/, stdlib unittest only) -- the first in this codebase's history, 36 tests covering the new ASUP parser functions and the multi-account merge/config logic added in 5.0.0, including two tests that pin the exact real bugs found during that feature's live testing. All 36 tests pass.
